sentences.text: Stenomyti is an extinct genus of small aetosaurs, armored reptiles that thrived during the Late Triassic period.
The osteoderms of Stenomyti are nearly identical to those of Aetosaurus, suggesting that armor plates are not always reliable for distinguishing aetosaur species.
Fossils of Stenomyti huangae, including a skull and postcranial skeleton, were found in the Late Triassic Chinle Formation in the Eagle Basin of Colorado, United States.
Stenomyti belongs to the subfamily Aetosaurinae and is classified within the family Stagonolepididae.
Stenomyti lived during the Norian to Rhaetian stages of the Late Triassic, from 227.3 to 201.4 million years ago.
Researchers suggest that Stenomyti is closely related to Aetosaurus and lies outside the clades containing Typothoracisinae and Desmatosuchinae based on osteoderm and cranial similarities.
